Vanhamme2003Apolipoprotein.title: Apolipoprotein L-I Is the Trypanosome Lytic Factor of Human Serum
Vanhamme2003Apolipoprotein.core_contribution: Discovered that APOL1 is the specific trypanolytic factor conferring human innate immunity against Trypanosoma brucei brucei.

Genovese2010Association.title: Association of Trypanolytic ApoL1 Variants with Kidney Disease in African Americans
Genovese2010Association.core_contribution: Landmark paper identifying APOL1 G1/G2 variants that confer resistance to T. b. rhodesiense but drive high risk for FSGS and ESRD in African Americans.

Tzur2010Missense.title: Missense Mutations in the APOL1 Gene Are Highly Associated with End Stage Kidney Disease Risk Previously Attributed to the MYH9 Gene
Tzur2010Missense.core_contribution: Proved that missense variants in APOL1, not MYH9, account for chromosome 22-linked non-diabetic kidney disease risk in African Americans.

Kopp2011Genetic.title: APOL1 Genetic Variants in Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis and HIV-Associated Nephropathy
Kopp2011Genetic.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
Kopp2011Genetic.core_contribution: Quantified massive odds ratio elevation for FSGS (OR 17) and HIVAN (OR 29) under recessive APOL1 risk allele inheritance.

Parsa2013Risk.title: APOL1 Risk Variants, Race, and Progression of Chronic Kidney Disease
Parsa2013Risk.core_contribution: Demonstrated that two APOL1 risk alleles account for the accelerated CKD progression previously attributed generally to racial disparity.

Genovese2013Variants.title: APOL1 Variants and Kidney Disease in People of Recent African Ancestry
Genovese2013Variants.core_contribution: Synthesized the early genetic mapping, selective sweep dynamics, and broad clinical consequences across glomerular pathologies.

Thomson2014Evolution.title: Evolution of the Primate Trypanolytic Factor APOL1
Thomson2014Evolution.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Thomson2014Evolution.core_contribution: Uncovered molecular mechanism of SRA evasion whereby deletion/mutations in APOL1 risk alleles neutralize parasite resistance factor.

Limou2014Population.title: APOL1 Kidney Risk Alleles: Population Genetics and Disease Associations
Limou2014Population.core_contribution: Mapped global frequencies and evolutionary haplotypes of APOL1 G1/G2 variants across African continental and diaspora groups.

Freedman2016Genotype.title: APOL1 Genotype and Kidney Transplantation Outcomes from Deceased African American Donors
Freedman2016Genotype.core_contribution: Established that donor APOL1 high-risk genotypes significantly diminish deceased-donor renal allograft survival.

Olabisi2016Cytotoxicity.title: APOL1 Kidney Disease Risk Variants Cause Cytotoxicity by Depleting Cellular Potassium and Inducing Stress-Activated Protein Kinases
Olabisi2016Cytotoxicity.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Olabisi2016Cytotoxicity.core_contribution: Identified toxic ion channel activity causing potassium efflux and activating stress-activated kinases (p38 MAPK/JNK) as the molecular driver of APOL1 injury.

Beckerman2017Transgenic.title: Transgenic Expression of Human APOL1 Risk Variants in Podocytes Induces Kidney Disease in Mice
Beckerman2017Transgenic.core_contribution: Created podocyte-specific inducible transgenic mouse model confirming that G1/G2 expression triggers autophagic disruption, podocyte depletion, and glomerulosclerosis in vivo.

KruzelDavila2017Trafficking.title: APOL1-Mediated Cell Injury Involves Disruption of Conserved Trafficking Processes
KruzelDavila2017Trafficking.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
KruzelDavila2017Trafficking.core_contribution: Demonstrated that APOL1 risk variants impair conserved endosomal and vesicular trafficking machinery, leading to cytotoxicity.

Freedman2018Disparities.title: APOL1-Associated Nephropathy: A Key Contributor to Racial Disparities in CKD
Freedman2018Disparities.core_contribution: Integrated genetic, pathologic, and clinical evidence highlighting APOL1 as the principal genetic determinant of racial disparities in non-diabetic CKD.

Aghajan2019Antisense.title: Antisense Oligonucleotide Treatment Ameliorates IFN-gamma-Induced Proteinuria in APOL1-Transgenic Mice
Aghajan2019Antisense.core_contribution: Provided first preclinical proof-of-concept that silencing APOL1 with antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) reduces proteinuria.

Friedman2020Genetics.title: APOL1 and Kidney Disease: From Genetics to Biology
Friedman2020Genetics.core_contribution: Authoritative review synthesizing channel function, membrane pore insertion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and toxic gain-of-function cascades.

Friedman2021Clinical.title: APOL1 Nephropathy: From Genetics to Clinical Applications
Friedman2021Clinical.journal: Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
Friedman2021Clinical.core_contribution: Outlines practical guidelines for APOL1 testing in clinical practice, living kidney donor risk assessment, and clinical trial stratifications.

Daneshpajouhnejad2022Evolving.title: The Evolving Story of Apolipoprotein L1 Nephropathy: The End of the Beginning
Daneshpajouhnejad2022Evolving.core_contribution: Comprehensive review examining two-hit inflammatory signaling, structural biophysics, and the emerging drug pipeline for AMKD.

Egbuna2023Inaxaplin.title: Inaxaplin for Proteinuric Kidney Disease in Persons with Two APOL1 Variants
Egbuna2023Inaxaplin.core_contribution: Landmark trial showing first targeted small-molecule APOL1 inhibitor (inaxaplin/VX-147) achieved 47.6% reduction in proteinuria at 13 weeks in FSGS patients.
